claims.claim: 95 מקרי טבח - רק השנה (95 massacre incidents in Colombia in 2026 so far)
claims.verified_figure: INDEPAZ running tally: the 1 Oct 2026 killing of four men near Cartagena (Tierra Baja–Puerto Rey) was registered as masacre #95 of 2026; the 4 Oct 2026 Santander de Quilichao (Cauca) attack, 3 killed, was registered as #96 (reported 5 Oct). Prior: 94 as of 30 Sep (Sevilla, Valle); 78 in all of 2025. INDEPAZ definition: intentional, simultaneous killing of 3+ defenceless people by the same perpetrator in the same time/manner/place. The state CNMH registry counts from 4+ victims, so an official count would be lower. The US Embassy Bogota advisory (Level 3, March 2026) and security alerts (Cesar 3 Sep; Norte de Santander 29 Sep 2026) are the source for the explosive-drone element, but are not the origin of the '95' figure (a March-period advisory snapshot cited 47).
claims.article_figure_per_search_snippet: 95 (headline). Body not readable (EGRESS_BLOCKED). A search result showed the same article ID (ddc5f9da52701a1027) under mako travel-news with a different title ('"תקיפות ללא התראה": אזהרה חמורה למדינה היפה'). A search-engine summary of the Hebrew coverage attributes the 95th massacre to Indepaz and ties it to the Cartagena shooting.
claims.note: In scope: this is an NGO running tally with a contested definition (3+ victims under INDEPAZ/UN usage vs 4+ under CNMH), not a fixed official registry. 95 matches INDEPAZ exactly for 1–4 Oct 2026, and 'רק השנה' (2026 to date) is the correct window. Caveats: (1) the headline does not attribute the figure. Placing it next to 'travel warning' suggests it comes from the warning, but it is INDEPAZ's count. (2) The 3+ definition is not stated. (3) The count was already 96 by 5 Oct, so the number is a slightly stale snapshot, not an error. The secondary claim that groups 'began' using rigged drones overstates the novelty. Armed groups have used explosive drones in Catatumbo and Cauca since 2024, and the US Embassy alerts describe repeated use. This is noted only and not scored as a data claim.
